what_it_checks: The same bank transaction arriving in more than one load. int_payments keeps only the first copy, so this is a warning, not a failure, but someone should tell the bank.
After deduplication, one row per bank transaction.

Voice calls only inside each market's calling window, in the customer's local time: UAE 09:00 to 20:00 Monday to Friday (Central Bank consumer protection rules), UK 08:00 to 21:00 and Spain and Mexico 09:00 to 21:00, Monday to Saturday, as our stated policy where the regulator only says "not at unreasonable times". Never on a Sunday. It has to use local time: in UTC a 10:00 call in Mexico City looks like a 16:00 call.
We never collect more than the account owed.

Every bank's monthly collections, converted to euros and back, land on the local total straight from the bank files. It compares against the source on purpose: a join that drops rows also drops them from any total taken after it, so only the source shows the gap. This is the check that found the missing weekend payments.
Every payment converts to euros. A payment without a rate silently disappears from any euro total, which is exactly what happened to weekend payments before I fixed the join.
Each account is in one variant, and every call it got used that variant's agent version.
Weekdays with no published rate. Usually a bank holiday. The daily rate table carries the last rate forward, but a long gap is worth a look.
A promise's instalments add up to the promised total.
No calls on a public holiday in the customer's market.
Nothing is sent to a customer before the bank placed the account with us.
Every loaded payment row has its own id.
The marts do not lose or invent money: collected per bank per month in the KPI table equals the deduplicated payments.
A reversal points to a real payment on the same account and never returns more than was paid.
